title: Admin - Comment Moderation - AI Offensive Language Detection - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Comment Moderation - AI Offensive Language Detection feature on the Y4J platform. This system feature detects offensive or prohibited keywords in user content, highlights them as red badges, provides Device Matcher Notes explaining the flagging reason, marks content as 'Needs Review', and requires admin manual approval or rejection. Covers keyword highlighting, notes display, status marking, admin actions, and edge cases.

testCases.title: Offensive keywords are highlighted as red badges
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A moderation item with detected offensive keywords exists.
steps: Find a card that has been flagged for offensive language
Observe the content text area on the card
expectedResults: Offensive keywords within the content are highlighted
The highlighting uses red badges/tags to mark the offensive words
The badges are visually distinct from normal text
Multiple offensive words are each individually highlighted
The surrounding context text remains readable
testCases.postconditions: Offensive keywords are confirmed highlighted as red badges

testCases.title: Device Matcher Notes explain the reason for flagging
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A moderation item flagged by AI exists.
steps: Find a card flagged by the AI/Device Matcher
Locate the Device Matcher Notes section on the card
expectedResults: Device Matcher Notes are displayed on the flagged card
The notes explain WHY the content was flagged (e.g., 'Contains offensive language: [word]')
The explanation is clear and actionable for the admin
The notes are labeled as AI/Device Matcher generated
testCases.postconditions: Device Matcher Notes are confirmed visible with explanation

testCases.title: Flagged content is marked as 'Needs Review'
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content with offensive keywords has been submitted.
steps: Find a card that was flagged by the AI system
Observe the status badge on the card
expectedResults: The flagged content shows 'Needs Review' status badge
The status is automatically set by the system (not manually)
The item appears when filtering by 'Pending' status
The status clearly indicates admin action is required

testCases.title: Admin can approve flagged content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A flagged item with 'Needs Review' status exists.
steps: Find a flagged item with 'Needs Review' status
expectedResults: An 'Approve' action is available on the flagged card
Clicking Approve changes the status to 'Approved'
The content becomes visible to users after approval
A success notification may be displayed
The admin's decision overrides the AI flag
testCases.postconditions: Flagged content is approved and visible to users

testCases.title: Admin can reject flagged content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A flagged item with 'Needs Review' status exists.
steps: Find a flagged item with 'Needs Review' status
expectedResults: A 'Reject' action is available on the flagged card
Clicking Reject changes the status to 'Rejected'
The content remains hidden from users
A success notification may be displayed
The rejection is recorded
testCases.postconditions: Flagged content is rejected and hidden from users

testCases.title: Admin must manually approve or reject - no auto-action
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Flagged content exists.
steps: Verify the content remains in 'Needs Review' until admin takes action
expectedResults: Flagged content stays in 'Needs Review' indefinitely until admin acts
The system does NOT auto-approve or auto-reject flagged content
Manual admin intervention is required
The content is not visible to users while in 'Needs Review' state

testCases.title: Multiple offensive keywords are each highlighted individually
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content with multiple offensive keywords exists.
steps: Find a card with content containing multiple offensive words
expectedResults: Each offensive keyword is individually highlighted with a red badge
Multiple badges appear if multiple words are flagged
The Device Matcher Notes may list all flagged words
Non-offensive words between flagged words are not highlighted

testCases.title: Red badge styling is clearly visible and accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Flagged content with red badges exists.
steps: Find a card with red keyword badges
expectedResults: Red badges have sufficient contrast against the background
The badge text (offensive word) is readable within the badge
The red color clearly indicates a warning/flag
The badges do not break the card layout
testCases.postconditions: Red badges are visually clear and accessible

testCases.title: Flagged items appear in Pending filter
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. AI-flagged items exist.
expectedResults: AI-flagged items with 'Needs Review' status appear in the Pending filter
They are grouped with other pending items
The flagged items show their red badges and Device Matcher Notes
They are distinguishable from non-AI-flagged pending items
testCases.postconditions: Flagged items are accessible via Pending filter

testCases.title: Content without offensive keywords is not flagged
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Clean content (no offensive keywords) exists.
steps: Find a card with clean content (no offensive language)
expectedResults: No red badges are displayed on clean content
No Device Matcher Notes section appears
The content may have 'Ready to Approve' status (not 'Needs Review' from AI)
The AI system correctly identifies non-offensive content
testCases.postconditions: Clean content is confirmed not flagged

testCases.title: Obfuscated offensive words are detected (edge case)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content with obfuscated offensive words (e.g., 'sc@mmer') has been submitted.
steps: Look for content with obfuscated offensive words
Observe if the AI detected and flagged them
expectedResults: Obfuscated words (e.g., 'sc@mmer', 'h8te') are detected by the AI
They are highlighted with red badges
Device Matcher Notes explain the detection
OR if not detected, this is documented as a known limitation

testCases.title: Mixed language abuse is detected (edge case)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content with mixed language offensive text has been submitted.
steps: Look for content with mixed language abuse
Observe if the AI detected and flagged it
expectedResults: Mixed language offensive content is detected by the AI
It is flagged with appropriate badges and notes
OR if not detected, this is documented as a known limitation
The system handles multilingual content gracefully
